title: lathyrus ochraceus subsp. hispanicus
intro: Lathyrus ochraceus subsp. hispanicus, commonly known as Spanish pease vetch or Spanish vetchling, is a perennial legume plant that belongs to the Fabaceae family. It has been used for centuries in traditional medicine due to its potential health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties. The therapeutic actions of this plant are attributed to its ability to modulate the immune system, exhibit wound-healing properties, and exhibit anticancer activities, which are thought to be triggered by its bioactive constituents, including flavonoids, alkaloids, and phenolic acids. Additionally, the plant's antioxidant properties are thought to be beneficial in protecting against oxidative stress and cell damage, while its antimicrobial properties may help to prevent infections and promote wound healing.
